newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: VKE seeks transparency over KPN/TNT acquisition.
newsitem.headline: VKE seeks transparency over KPN/TNT acquisition.

text.p: VKE, the Dutch courier and express association, has called for more transparency over Koninklijke PTT Nederland's (KPN) proposed acquisition of Australian express group TNT.

In a submission to the European Commission the group, which has 300 members including the major integrators, stressed that it is not against the acquisition but it wants to know more about how the Dutch postal and telecommunications group is financing the acquisition, said VKE secretary Ernst Gleym.
VKE argues that cross-subsidisation may be taking place because the postal group has enjoyed such a dominant position in the Dutch market.
"We would like to know where exactly the money is coming from," Gleym stated.
KPN has a monopoly in the letters (up to 500gram) market and we want to know whether this position is being abused to acquire companies such as TNT, he added.
"We want to see more control and have better information," he said.

VKE argues that the Dutch government is not being given enough information by KPN and therefore cannot find out if cross-subsidiation is going on, with money from its monopoly being used for acquisitions.
"If they are to keep their postal monopoly we need more control and transparency of information," Gleym said.
